set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-later; milestone-maintenance.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: Acceptance retained; this audit did not run its proposed tests.

Remaining / next action: Wait for a concrete consumer and ADR before adding a contiguity-checked grouping claim. Existing Coarsening is intentionally order-free; legitimate reverse cuts must not be rejected as non-monotone.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Scheduling lane: later. Governing plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19: Coarsening remains deliberately order-free. No defect or new public claim without a concrete consumer and ADR; unrelated to the preview.

Historical finding and scope retained below; current acceptance ownership above governs.

LinkClaim.Coarsening admits a non-contiguous grouping: {1->2, 2->1, 3->2} is accepted, though no cut order produces it (the preimage of target 2 is {1,3}). It was pinned deliberately at 41c1338f as the honest boundary of the claim; Coarsening promises only "many to one, every target reached, nothing dropped".

The monotonicity check a reviewer proposed is correctly refused: it would refuse Memento, which is cut in reverse and is legitimately non-monotone. The ORDER-FREE check that separates the two cases is preimage contiguity: a genuine reverse cut {1->2, 2->2, 3->1} is preimage-contiguous, and the scrambled case is not.

This is a question for later, not a defect: is a contiguity-checked claim wanted (a new LinkClaim case, or a checked property of Coarsening)? That is new vocabulary, so ADR first (SD5). Low priority until a corpus needs it.
